en: The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Merit Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and State Preceptor for Enlightened Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"You should listen attentively; I shall now, for your sake and for the sake of sentient beings in the age of the final dharma, proclaim the dhāraṇī of immeasurable merit."
You should keep this in mind and never forget it,
so that in the future age of defilement and evil,
you may bring about great and wholesome benefit for all sentient beings.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī and recite it twenty-one times every morning,
all the evil karma accumulated by those persons over a thousand kalpas will be completely extinguished.
One will see that one's own body attains peace and happiness.
If a person recites this with a sincere mind for one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*),
that person shall, in a future life, behold the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
If one recites it two hundred thousand times,
one shall come to behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
if one recites it three hundred thousand times, [the same result follows].
In the future, one shall behold Amitāyus Buddha. Then he spoke this dhāraṇī: *Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo 'rha*...
*Āryāmitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya tadyathā amite amitodbhave* (7) *ame*...
1. *Ryā* (2) *amita* (3) *ābhāya* (4) *tathāgatāya* (5) *arhat* (6) *samyaḳsaṃbuddhāya* (7) *tadyathā* (8) *amite* (9) *amitodbhave* (10) *ame* (11) *a*.
mitrasvāmi (8) amitavikrānti (9) amitavikrāntagamiṇi (10) gaganagañjodgata (11) sarvakleśa (12) kṣaṇa.
*Jvalaye svāhā.* (13) At that time, Ānanda,
having heard the Tathāgata speak this dhāraṇī of immeasurable merit, [was filled with joy].
Rejoicing, they accepted it with faith, prostrated to the Buddha, and withdrew.
The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of Immeasurable Merit Spoken by the Buddha.
